(2) Members of appointed boards, commissions, authorities and judges.
(3) Persons employed or appointed to conduct temporary and special inquiry, investigation or examination on behalf of the elected officials.
(4) Incumbents of any position designated as excepted, which because of its nature cannot or should not be appropriately included in the covered category.
(5) Employees in Georgia Merit System positions.
(6) Persons performing work under contract.
(Code 2003, § 2-7002; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 1)
545:
Excepted employees shall have their pay and other conditions of employment established individually by the elected officials authorized to appoint employees in the department where the excepted position is authorized.
(Code 2003, § 2-7003; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 2)
546:
The City Council shall designate an equal employment opportunity (EEO) officer, who is ultimately responsible for the administration of these rules. The EEO Officer may delegate, as necessary, to department heads, managers and supervisors, the responsibility for administering these rules. The EEO Officer shall notify the City Council within three working days of any disciplinary action or adverse action taken against any department head.
(Code 2003, § 2-7004; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 3)
547:
These rules may be amended at any regular or special meeting of the City Council by adoption of an appropriate amendment. Proposed changes shall be submitted to other elected officials for their consideration at least one week prior to the meeting.
(Code 2003, § 2-7005; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 4)
548:
Employees covered by this plan are classed as full-time, part-time, temporary and irregular.
(1) Full-time employees are those appointed to continuing positions who work 30 or more hours per week.
(2) Part-time employees are those appointed to continuing positions who work less than 30 hours per week.
(3) Temporary employees are those who are employed in positions not authorized to exceed one year; or who are employed in continuing positions, but their period of employment is scheduled for less than one year. Temporary employees may be full-time or part-time.
(4) Irregular employees are those who are hired on a year-round basis and are subject to call to fill occasionally for regular employees or during peak workload periods.
(Code 2003, § 2-7006; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 5)
549:
(a) Overtime shall be defined as any hours in excess of any employee's standard workweek, as established by the City Council. Overtime shall be paid at 1½ times the employee's standard hourly rate.
(b) Employees will not work in excess of their established duty hours unless authorized. Employees who work overtime without advance approval will not be entitled to overtime pay.
(Code 2003, § 2-7007; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 6)
550:
(a) The following holidays are observed:
(1) January 1.
(2) Martin Luther King, Jr. Birthday.
(3) July 4.
(4) Labor Day.
(5) Veterans Day.
(6) Thanksgiving Day.
(7) Christmas.
(b) All full-time employees scheduled for duty on a holiday, and whose duties permit, will receive the holidays off with pay. Full-time employees who are required to work on a holiday will receive double their regular pay or compensatory time off, at the option of the employer.
(Code 2003, § 2-7008; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 7; Mo. of 1-15-1991; Mo. of 11-5-2002)
551:
(a) Full-time employees only are entitled to vacation leave. Vacation leave may be approved to cover vacation, emergency absence, and sick leave after all earned sick leave is exhausted.
(b) Employees are not entitled to vacation leave during the first 12 months of employment. Employees will be credited with leave as follows:
(1) After one year's employment. Employees will be credited with leave equal to the number of regularly scheduled days and hours in the standard work or duty week to which the employee is assigned at the time the vacation leave is granted.
(2) After three years' employment. Employees will be granted leave equal to two times the number of days and hours in their standard work or duty week to which assigned at the time the vacation leave is granted.
(3) After ten years' employment. Employees will be granted leave equal to three times the number of days and hours in their standard work or duty week to which assigned at the time vacation leave is granted.
(4) After 20 years continuous employment. Employees will be granted leave of four weeks.
(c) Employees must schedule vacation leave during the year in which it is credited.
(d) After one year of employment, employees leaving the service of this government will be paid for unused vacation leave to their credit.
(Code 2003, § 2-7009; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 8)
552:
(a) Full-time employees only are entitled to sick leave. In order to be entitled to sick leave, an employee must be incapacitated for work due to illness, pregnancy, a non-job-connected injury, or have a doctor's or dentist's appointment. Employees who are absent frequently for short periods of illness, or who are out sick over three days, may be required to produce a doctor's statement attesting to the illness or disability.
(b) Employees will not be paid for sick leave during the first 12 months of employment. After 12 months' employment, employees will earn sick leave at the rate of two weeks per year. Sick leave not used during the year it is credited may be accumulated up to a maximum of 26 weeks.
(c) Employees will not be paid for unused sick leave to their credit on leaving the service of this government.
(Code 2003, § 2-7010; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 9)
553:
(a) Administrative leave is paid time off granted for any purpose which benefits both the employee and the government. Administrative leave with pay will be granted for such purposes as:
(1) Reserve military training as required by O.C.G.A. § 38-2-279.
(2) Jury duty, or as a witness for this government in any court.
(b) Maternity leave is paid time off due to pregnancy and is charged against sick leave time.
(c) Leave without pay is approved time off without pay at the employee's request or as directed by management, for justifiable purpose. An employee may be granted leave without pay for a period not to exceed three months. In the case of a medical disability, a doctor's certificate may be required certifying the employee's inability to work before leave without pay is approved.
(Code 2003, § 2-7011; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 1, § 10)
556:
(a) All newly hired permanent full-time employees will be required to serve a probationary period. During this period, the department head or elected official will evaluate the ability of new employees and determine their potential to make satisfactory long-term employees. It is a part of the examining process and is considered to be the last step in the selection of a new employee.
(b) The probationary period begins with the date of appointment as a permanent full-time employee. The length of the probationary period is 12 months.
(Code 2003, § 2-7020; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 2, § 1)
557:
Employees will be closely observed during the probationary period. Their inabilities and deficiencies will be noted. Special attention will be given to counseling new employees on job deficiencies and an effort will be made to assist them in bringing their performance up to satisfactory. If, at any time up to the date the probationary period ends, it becomes apparent an employee will not make a satisfactory career worker, a dismissal action will be taken.
(Code 2003, § 2-7021; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 2, § 2)
558:
An employee who is to be dismissed will be notified in writing of the specific details causing dismissal, or that the reason is failure to qualify during the probationary period. The employee will be given the letter in person prior to the date of the separation, or prior to the last day of the probationary period. A probationary employee cannot appeal a dismissal action taken during the probationary period.
(Code 2003, § 2-7022; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 2, § 3)
561:
The purpose of this article is to establish a policy to be used by management in determining appropriate disciplinary action for employee infractions. The policy also establishes administrative procedures to be followed in taking disciplinary action and in processing adverse actions against full-time employees. The schedule of offenses and penalties (Section 40-208) informs employees and supervisors of the range and types of penalties recommended for breaches of discipline committed by employees.
(Code 2003, § 2-7030; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3)
562:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Adverse action means the procedure which must be followed when dismissing or demoting a full-time employee who has completed the probationary period.
Disciplinary action means and includes written reprimand, suspending an employee from duty without pay, demotion and dismissal.
Non-duty status with pay means placing an employee in a non-work status away from the job while continuing the employee's regular pay. This is only used while investigating an employee to determine if dismissal action is warranted and the employee's presence on the job is believed to constitute a hazard to the employee or others. It shall be done by letter giving the reason and contain instructions concerning contacts with this government during this period. It is not a disciplinary action.
(Code 2003, § 2-7031; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3)
563:
The use of the disciplinary and adverse action procedures and schedule of penalties and offenses prescribed herein applies to all full-time employees who have completed their probationary period. Probationary full-time, part-time, temporary and excepted employees are not covered by this policy. Unless protected by some other policy, regulation or law, they may be separated at any time without advance notice or appeal.
(Code 2003, § 2-7032; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 1)
564:
The schedule is intended to assist supervisors in determining how to discipline employees and at the same time correct their work habits or behavior in such a way that they can be retained as useful workers. Dismissal action should be taken on the first offense only for serious misconduct or when it becomes apparent that several lesser penalties have failed to rehabilitate a chronic offender.
(Code 2003, § 2-7033; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 2)
565:
(a) The schedule is flexible since it recognizes that the selection of a penalty in any specific case will depend on the type of offense and how serious it is. It must also take into account the effect it will have on this government, other employees, and the public. Consideration must be given the employee's authority, seniority, past employment history, and the circumstances which led to the infraction. In many cases, for the first minor offense, the supervisor may decide to only caution and counsel the employee.
(b) For most offenses, the schedule provides several levels of severity to choose from with respect to a penalty. This gives the responsible supervisor several alternative actions for each successive infraction. The least harsh penalty which the supervisor believes will have the desired corrective effect on the employee will normally be imposed. A penalty within the range shown for that number of offenses on the chart (Section 40-208) should be used. Example: first offense, second offense, third offense. It is not intended that for a series of minor offenses the penalty for the third offense must always be dismissal. Again, the primary consideration is judging whether or not the employee can be rehabilitated and what effect on the total organization the action will have.
(Code 2003, § 2-7034; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 3)
566:
The following penalties may be imposed:
(1) Written reprimand is the lightest penalty. A letter signed by the department head or elected official will be given to the employee advising this is a written reprimand and what offense it is being given for. It will also state whether it is the first, second, third or fourth penalty imposed. The letter should warn that further infractions may lead to suspension or dismissal. A copy of the letter will be filed in the employee's personnel folder.
(2) Suspension is a severe penalty. The employee may be suspended from work without pay for from one day, not to exceed ten days, depending on the seriousness of the offense. This must be done by letter in advance of the first day of suspension giving the reason and what day the employee is to report back to work. The letter will be signed by the department head and warn that further infractions may lead to dismissal. A copy will be filed in the employee's personnel folder.
(3) Demotion is not normally used as a disciplinary action. It is more appropriate in those cases where the employee fails to perform satisfactorily because of inability rather than indolence. Providing the employee is otherwise satisfactory, and there is another position at a lower level that it is believed the employee can perform, the demotion action serves as a useful purpose. The employee will be notified in writing at least ten days in advance of the date of demotion. The letter will be signed by the EEO Officer. It will contain the specific reasons for the action, the date of the demotion, and inform the employee of the employee's right to appeal the action. (See Article IV of this Chapter, Adverse Action Appeals.) A copy will be filed in the employee's personnel folder.
(4) Dismissal is the final penalty. The employee will be notified in writing at least ten workdays in advance of the date of separation. The letter should be delivered or mailed in advance of the beginning of the ten workdays period. The letter will be signed by the EEO Officer and will include in detail the specific reason for the dismissal, the date of separation, and inform the employee of any appeal rights. If should also inform the employee that if the employee is going to appeal, the date by which the appeal must be received. (See Article IV of this Chapter, Adverse Action Appeals.) A copy of the letter will be filed in the employee's personnel folder.
(Code 2003, § 2-7035; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 4)
567:
(a) Normally, disciplinary action shall be initiated within one week after an offense has been committed or discovered. For extremely serious offenses, action may be taken as soon as management becomes aware of the infraction, regardless of the period of time which has elapsed since the offense occurred.
(b) In assessing a penalty for a current offense which has been preceded by several other offenses for which a disciplinary penalty has been given, only those disciplinary actions taken within the three-year period just prior to the date of the current infraction may be used to justify a more severe penalty.
(Code 2003, § 2-7036; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 5)
568:
(a) Department heads are delegated authority to impose the following disciplinary penalties on employees under their supervision: Written reprimand and suspension without pay.
(b) Authority to place an employee in a nonduty status with pay, and to take adverse actions involving demotion or dismissal charges against an employee rests with the EEO Officer. Department heads may recommend such action.
(c) The Personnel Director, as specified in the City Natural Gas Department Anti-Drug Program's Policies and Procedures, shall have the authority and is hereby given the authority to discharge any employee of the gas department instanter upon such employee testing positive to drugs as defined in the policies and procedures and for any violation of the Natural Gas Department's Anti-Drug Policies and Procedures as adopted by the City.
(Code 2003, § 2-7037; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 6; Ord. of 2-5-1991)
569:
A schedule of offenses and penalties is set forth in Section 40-208. It is impossible to include every type of disciplinary problem which may arise, or describe every situation explicitly. For those not found in Section 40-208, supervisors should compare the unlisted offense with those listed and select the one most similar or of comparable seriousness. Apply the penalty to the unlisted offense in a like manner.
(Code 2003, § 2-7038; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 7)
570:
(a) Letters to employees proposing demotion or dismissal will contain the date of the proposed action and the reason for the action. These reasons will be specific and in detail and contain all facts being relied on to support the action. Nothing concerning prior disciplinary actions will be included in this paragraph of the letter.
(b) In the next paragraph make reference to prior disciplinary actions, if any, taken against the employee, only if required by the schedule of offenses and penalties to justify the severity of the penalty proposed. Use only those occurring within the three years immediately prior to the date the current offense occurred, and for which a penalty was imposed. Briefly state the offense, the penalty imposed and date of each charge used.
(c) In this paragraph, advise that if the employee desires to appeal the action, the date by which the appeal must be received (no later than the third workday following receipt of this letter). Include a statement that the appeal must be in writing and be received by the EEO Officer no later than the third workday following receipt of this letter, and that if a timely appeal is not received, no further notice of the dismissal will be given.
(d) If at all possible, the letter should be delivered to the employee in person. When this is not possible, send by certified mail to the last known address and allow one extra day for receiving the appeal.
(e) The letter must be dated, signed, and delivered in advance of the ten-day required notice period.
(Code 2003, § 2-7039; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 3, § 8)
573:
The purpose of this article is to provide an administrative procedure for processing appeals concerning demotion and dismissal actions and seek to have these decisions set aside. Appeals concerning other disciplinary actions shall be handled under the procedures set forth in Article V of this Chapter, Grievance Procedure.
(Code 2003, § 2-7040; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 4)
574:
This procedure may be used by all full-time employees who have completed their probationary period. Excepted, temporary and part-time employees are not entitled to use this procedure. These employees are encouraged to discuss such actions with their immediate superior.
(Code 2003, § 2-7041; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 4, § 1)
575:
(a) An employee may appeal a demotion or dismissal action. The appeal must be in writing and be received in the EEO Officer's office no later than the close of business (5:00 p.m.) on the third workday following receipt of the letter of notification; otherwise, it will not be accepted. The day the letter of notification is given the employee is not included in this three-day period. Upon receiving an appeal, the employee will be given a copy of this adverse action appeals procedures and advised to comply with it.
(b) Employees have the right to be accompanied, advised and represented by a person of their own choosing in presenting their appeal under this procedure.
(c) Management will normally be represented by the department head over the employee. However, the EEO Officer may designate another person to be management's representative.
(d) Both the employee and management are entitled to submit pertinent documentary evidence and witnesses in support of their positions. It is the responsibility of each party to arrange for their own witnesses and representatives to attend the scheduled administrative hearing. The board will maintain a file of accepted documentary evidence.
(e) The appeals board will set the time and place of the hearing. If conducted during their working hours, all employees required to be present will be in a pay status during the period they are in attendance. This also covers the aggrieved and any employees called by this party.
(f) The aggrieved and any employee representative and witnesses shall be free from reprisal or harassment for appearing on behalf of the aggrieved.
(Code 2003, § 2-7042; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 4, § 2)
576:
An appeals board will be formed to conduct the administrative hearing. The board will consist of three members: One selected by the governing body; one selected by the appealing employee, and a third selected by these two members. These members should be selected and the EEO Officer notified of the selection within three working days after the appeal is received from the aggrieved employee. The member appointed by the governing body will chair the appeals board and convene the administrative hearing. Failure of the aggrieved employee to select a board member, or cause this member to appear for any called meeting, shall not be reason to delay the procedure, and the governing body member may proceed with the arrangements for the hearing without this member's presence. It is the aggrieved employee's responsibility to have the employee's appointed board member present. In the event the aggrieved employee refuses or fails to select a board member, the governing body member may select the employee member.
(Code 2003, § 2-7043; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 4, § 3)
577:
(a) The administrative hearing will be an informal procedure. Formal or judicial procedures such as rules of evidence, objections to testimony or introduction of documentary evidence, challenges of witnesses, sworn testimony, or cross examination of witnesses by either party will not be allowed.
(b) The appeals board shall open the hearing as soon as possible after appointment, normally within three days, to obtain evidence and testimony. The board will interview both parties and their witnesses, and accept documentary evidence.
(c) The appeals board may go into closed session any time it determines this is necessary. It will continue the hearing until such time it is satisfied it has information on which to reach a decision. The board will then go into closed session until such time the decision is reached. The board should attempt to complete the administrative hearing in one day.
(d) For all decisions, a majority vote of the board members prevails.
(e) Verbatim transcripts or summaries of testimony are not required.
(f) The appeals board will submit its written findings and recommendations to the EEO Officer as soon as possible, normally within one day following the close of the hearing.
(Code 2003, § 2-7044; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 4, § 4)
580:
It is the purpose of this article to establish a fair and impartial procedure by which employees may make known their complaints and dissatisfaction about conditions of employment and have bona fide complaints adjusted.
(Code 2003, § 2-7050; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 5)
581:
(a) A grievance is any complaint or dispute concerning such things as the interpretation of established personnel policies, working conditions, rules and regulations, disciplinary action (except demotion or dismissal), and charges of discrimination based on political affiliation, race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age or handicap. Certain management rights are excluded from coverage under this policy. They are:
(1) Dismissal during the probationary period;
(2) Grade level of position;
(3) Rate of pay; and
(4) Performance evaluation.
(b) Appeals concerning demotion and dismissal actions shall be handled under the procedures set forth in Section 40-208.
(Code 2003, § 2-7051; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 5)
582:
This procedure may be used by all full-time employees. It is not available to temporary, part-time or volunteer employees. These employees are encouraged to discuss any problem with their immediate supervisor.
(Code 2003, § 2-7052; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 5, § 1)
583:
Employees must verbally notify their department heads (or the elected official over the department when that official is the immediate supervisor), about the complaint. This must be done within three days after the matter arises, otherwise the complaint will not be acted upon. A complaint may be submitted on a continuing condition or action at any time.
(Code 2003, § 2-7053; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 5, § 2)
584:
(a) Step 1. The department head or elected official to whom the complaint is first submitted will meet with the employee no later than three workdays after receiving the notice and discuss the complaint. The employee will be advised verbally in person of the decision no later than three workdays following the discussion.
(b) Step 2. If the employee is not satisfied with the Step 1 decision, and the person who acted on the Step 1 decision was not an elected official, the complaint may be continued to Step 2. The complaint must be submitted within three workdays after receiving the Step 1 decision. The elected official over the department, (or the governing body), will meet with the employee within three days after receiving notification to discuss that complaint. The employee will be advised verbally in person of the decision no later than three days following the meeting. This decision is final.
(Code 2003, § 2-7054; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 5, § 3)
587:
Employees are expected to conduct themselves, both on and off the job, in a manner which will reflect favorably upon themselves and this government. Although this government does not wish to interfere in the private lives of its employees, they are expected to be honest, reliable, trustworthy, and of good character and reputation. Employees are expected to be loyal to this government. The following rules of conduct set forth in general what is expected of employees.
(Code 2003, § 2-7060; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6)
588:
Good taste will dictate employees' conduct. Courtesy and good manners are basic to good relations, both on and off the job. Violations of these two principles could lead to breaches of good conduct which may result in suspension or removal from the job.
(Code 2003, § 2-7061; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6, § 1)
589:
Every employee of this government should:
(1) Put loyalty to the highest moral principles and to this government above loyalty to persons, party or department.
(2) Uphold the Charter, ordinances, resolutions, and regulations of this government and never be a party to their evasion.
(3) Perform a full day's work for a full day's pay; giving to the performance of your duties your earnest effort and best thought.
(4) Seek to find and employ more efficient and economical ways of getting tasks accomplished.
(5) Never discriminate unfairly by the dispensing of special favors or privileges to anyone, whether for remuneration or not; and never accept, for self or family, favors or benefits under circumstances which might be construed by reasonable persons as influencing the performance of governmental duties.
(6) Make no private promise of any kind binding upon the duties of office, since a government employee has no private word which can be binding on public duty.
(7) Engage in no business with the government, either directly or indirectly, which is inconsistent with the conscientious performance of governmental duties.
(8) Never use any information received confidentially in the performance of governmental duties as a means for making private profit.
(9) Expose corruption wherever discovered.
(10) Uphold these principles, ever conscious that public office is a public trust.
(Code 2003, § 2-7062; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6, § 2)
590:
Employees are expected to observe the following rules and practices:
(1) Be at work on time, and observe the time limits established for meals and break periods.
(2) Do not leave work during duty hours without proper permission.
(3) Notify supervisors as soon as possible, but no later than one hour after starting time, if unable to report for work on time due to emergency or illness.
(4) Do not abuse sick leave privileges.
(5) Do not report for work under the influence of alcohol or intoxicating drugs, or use them on duty.
(6) Obey all proper orders from superiors. Insubordination includes refusal to obey instruction, use of abusive, profane or threatening language towards supervisory personnel.
(7) Do not coerce or harass fellow employees, or use profane or insulting language or gestures toward them.
(8) Do not engage in arguing, fighting, horseplay, or conduct violating common decency or morality.
(9) Do not bring firearms or other weapons to work, except after being given proper permission, or when required by your position.
(10) When required by the position, report for duty in a clean, neat, correct uniform.
(11) Do not sleep on duty unless authorized.
(12) Do not use government tools or equipment for personal use or remove them from government premises or control without proper permission.
(13) Gambling on duty or on government property is forbidden.
(14) Do not knowingly give false information on reports or other required documents.
(15) Maintain personal hygiene so as not to offend fellow workers.
(16) Do not knowingly violate any safety procedure or practice. Perform work so as to protect against accidents to self and others.
(17) Always observe all proper rules, regulations, policies, guides and laws in effect which are issued, or require compliance, by this government.
(Code 2003, § 2-7063; Ord. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6, § 3)
591:
(a) No employee may engage in any paid employment in addition to this employment which interferes with the efficient performance of the employee's duties and/or which presents a conflict of interest. Outside employment must be approved in advance.
(b) If outside employment creates a conflict-of-interest situation between the employee and this government, that employee will be expected to resign one of the positions the employee holds. Failure to comply with this regulation will constitute grounds for dismissal.
(Code 2003, § 2-7064; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6, § 4)
592:
An employee shall not accept gifts, gratuities or loans from organizations, business concerns or individuals with whom the employee has official relationships when representing this government. These limitations are not intended to prohibit the acceptance of articles of negligible value which are distributed generally, nor to prohibit employees from accepting social courtesies which promote good public relations, nor to prohibit employees from obtaining loans from regular lending institutions. It is particularly important that inspectors, contracting officers and enforcement officers guard against relationships which might be construed as evidence of favoritism, coercion, unfair advantage or collusion. Violations of this policy will result in disciplinary action.
(Code 2003, § 2-7065; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6. § 5)
593:
(a) No employee shall be appointed, promoted, demoted, favored or discriminated against with respect to employment in the personnel system because of the employee's political opinions or affiliations.
(b) No persons shall use or promise to use, directly or indirectly, any official authority or influence, whether possessed or anticipated, to secure or attempt to secure for any individual an appointment or advantage in appointment to a position in the personnel system or an increase in pay or other advantage in employment in any such position with the purpose of influencing the vote or political action of that individual.
(c) No employee in the personnel system shall, directly or indirectly, pay or promise to pay an assessment for political purposes, solicit or take any part in soliciting for any political party, or solicit or take any part in soliciting any political assessment, subscription, contribution, or service.
(d) No employee shall hold an elective office in this government, nor shall the employee solicit any contribution, assessments or service, nor shall the employee publicly endorse any candidate for an elective office in this government.
(e) Nothing herein contained shall affect the right of an employee to contribute to, hold membership in, serve as an officer of, support a political party, vote as the employee chooses, support or campaign for State or national political candidates, express privately the employee's opinions on all political subjects and candidates, maintain political neutrality or attend political meetings.
(f) Exceptions to the preceding Subsection (e) of this section. Any employee who, as a normal and foreseeable incident to the employee's principal job or position, performs duties in connection with an activity financed in whole or in part by federal loans and grants, comes under the Federal Hatch Act, which prohibits the following:
(1) Use of official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with an election or nomination for office, or affecting the result thereof.
(2) Directly or indirectly coercing, attempting to coerce, commanding or advising any other such officer or employee to pay, lend or contribute any part of the officer's or employee's salary or compensation or anything else of value to any party, committee, organization, agency or person for political purposes.
(3) Active participation in political party management or in political campaigns.
(Code 2003, § 2-7066; Mo. of 12-6-1980, pt. 6, § 6)
594:
The City, through its officers, agents and superintendents shall have the authority and duty to require any City employee under the City's direct supervision to submit to alcohol test and/or drug test upon such officer's suspicion that reasonable cause exist that such employee is on duty, working for the City, while having such substance in the employee's system. If such employee shall be found, through such test, to have a forbidden substance in the employee's system, or if such employee shall refuse to submit to such test at the time of request, the employee shall be presumed to be guilty of violating this section and shall be subject to the provisions of Sections 40-83 and 40-172(5); the City shall be responsible for the payment of the fees for the herein required test.
(Code 2003, § 2-7067; Ord. of 7-10-1990)
595:
(a) The United States Congress has enacted the Drug Free Workplace Act of 1988. The purpose of this law is to ensure that work done under federal contracts or federal grants is performed in a drug-free work environment. In addition to prohibiting employees from engaging in the unlawful manufacture, distribution, dispensation, possession, or use of illegal drugs in the workplace, this department prohibits its employees from engaging in such illegal activity at all times and at all places. Such activity, even during nonworking hours, clearly affects an employee's ability to perform the employee's public duties. Therefore, this City adopts the following as its drug-free policy:
(1) No employee of this City may illegally engage in the manufacture, distribution, dispensation, possession, or use of a controlled substance at any time or place, including while at the employee's workplace. Such unlawful activity will be considered a sufficient ground for a serious adverse personnel action, including dismissal from employment.

604:
(a) Scope. This article shall apply to all outdoor advertising signs abutting or visible from the limited access and primary highway rights-of-way in the City.
(b) Compliance. No sign shall be erected or maintained unless it is in compliance with the regulations of this article.
(c) Construction. Signs must be constructed of durable materials, maintained in good condition, and not permitted to become dilapidated.
(d) Location. All signs located on sites abutting or visible from a limited access highway or primary highway rights-of-way shall conform with O.C.G.A. title 32, ch. 6, art. 3, pt. 2 (O.C.G.A. § 32-6-70 et seq., the Georgia Outdoor Advertising Code), and shall meet all federal and State requirements necessary to obtain a permit under said code. In instances where the sign controls of this article are more strict, these regulations shall apply.
(e) Obsolete signs. Any sign which advertises an activity, business, product or service which has ceased operation or production shall be removed within six months of the discontinuance of said activity, business, product or service.
(Code 2003, § 8-6001; Ord. of 6-4-1985, § 1)
605:
(a) Home occupation signs. One nonilluminated professional or business nameplate not exceeding two square feet in area is permitted.
(b) Signs of work under construction. One nonilluminated sign not exceeding 40 square feet in area displaying the name of the building, the contractors, the architects, the engineers, the owners, the financial, selling and development agencies is permitted upon the premises of any work under the construction, alteration, or removal. Such signs shall be removed from the site within 30 days after the completion of the project.
(c) Temporary subdivision signs. Temporary signs, not exceeding 40 square feet in area announcing a land subdivision development are permitted on the premises of the land subdivision. Such signs shall be spaced not less than 300 feet apart. They shall be removed when 75 percent of the lots are conveyed.
(d) Roof signs. Not more than one roof sign structure may be erected on the roof of any one building. No roof sign structure shall extend more than 25 feet above the elevation of the roof.
(e) Wall signs.
(1) Generally. Signs on the walls of a building (including signs attached flat against the wall, painted wall signs and projecting signs) shall meet the following requirements:
a. Signs on the front surface of a building. The total area of signs on the exterior front surface of a building shall not exceed 25 percent of the front surface of the building.
b. Signs on the side and rear surfaces of a building. The total area of signs on a side or rear surface of a building shall not exceed 50 percent of the exterior side or rear surface of the building respectively.
c. Projecting signs. Wall signs attached flat against a wall may extend not more than 24 inches from the wall.
(2) Angle signs extending outward. Signs attached at an angle to a wall may extend outward from the wall of a building not more than five feet.
(f) Illuminated signs. Illumination devices shall be so placed and shielded that light from the sign itself will not directly cast into any residential district, sleeping rooms in any district or the eyes of an automobile or vehicle driver.
(g) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this subsection, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
On-premises signs means those signs which are located within 100 feet of a regularly used part of the business being advertised and on the same property.
Outdoor advertising signs means signs that do not meet the definition in Subsection (g)(1) of this section and that advertise a building, profession, product, service, activity, entertainment or any other advertisement not conducted, sold, or offered on the premises upon which the sign is located.
(h) Outdoor advertising signs visible from a limited access highway. Outdoor advertising signs visible from a limited access highway shall meet the following requirements:
(1) Uniform size. The outside measurements of all such signs shall be 12 feet in height and 50 feet in length, with or without trim.
(2) Illumination. All illuminated signs shall use base-mounted fluorescent or mercury vapor lights and shall be activated by photoelectric cells. Additional lighting, including, but not limited to, neon, animation and running lights is prohibited.
(3) Height above road grade. All signs shall be a minimum of ten feet above adjacent pavement measuring from the lower portion of the sign face. Signs shall not exceed 30 feet in height. Two signs in the same location (back to back) or "V" formation shall be the same height above the road's surface.
(4) Extrusions prohibited. Extrusions beyond the face of the sign, excluding aprons, are prohibited.
(5) Number of signs per location. Only one sign shall be allowed to face the same direction per location. This allows back to back or "V" formation signs but prohibits two signs (side by side) facing the same direction.
(6) Spacing. Sign locations shall be no less than 500 feet apart measuring from the two closest points.
(7) Sign structures. Sign structures shall be no less than ten feet from any property or right-of-way line.
(8) Number of signs allowed. Allow three outdoor advertising signs per quadrant of any interchange adjacent to the limited access highway. These signs must be within areas zoned commercial or industrial as specified in State law and are restricted to an area 1,200 feet long beginning 500 feet from the point where the pavement widens on the main traveled way to accommodate the longest entrance or exit ramp.
(9) Marsh and historic area locations prohibited. No sign shall be placed in or obstruct the view of a marshland area or an area of designated historic interest.
(10) Advertisement limitations.
a. Outdoor advertising shall be limited to the following:
1. Travel service facilities including lodgings, gas, food, camping;
2. Areas of scenic beauty;
3. Public attractions including historic, natural scientific or recreational amenities; and
4. Any combination of the above-listed facilities.
b. Further, the content of all advertising shall be directional in nature.
(i) Outdoor advertising signs visible from the primary highway system. Outdoor advertising signs visible from the primary highway system shall be located on commercial or industrial zoned property and shall also be located within 600 feet of an ongoing commercial or industrial establishment and shall not be located in an area which is primarily residential in nature. The provisions of Subsections (h)(2), (3), (4), (5), (6), (7) and (9) of this section are applicable to signs on the primary highways.
(j) On-premises signs near advertised activity. On-premises signs located within 100 feet of a regularly used part of the activity being advertised and located on the same property and for sale or for lease signs located on the property being advertised would not be prohibited.
(k) Nonconforming signs. Any legally erected sign which would become nonconforming as a result of this article would be allowed to remain until purchased by the department of transportation or the City, provided that the sign owner meets the requirements of State laws and rules and regulations governing such signs.
(Code 2003, § 8-6002; Ord. of 6-4-1985, § 3)

609:
(a) Definitions. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meaning ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Retail tire dealer means any person actively engaged in the business of selling new and used replacement tires.
Scrap tire means a tire that is no longer suitable for its original intended purpose because of wear, damage, or defect.
Scrap tire carrier means any person engaged in picking up or transporting scrap tires not otherwise exempted in the Georgia Rules for Solid Waste Management for the purpose of scrap tire processor, end user, or disposal facility.
Scrap tire generator means any person who generates scrap tires. The term "scrap tire generator" may include, but not be limited to, retail tire dealers, retreaders, scrap tire processors, automobile dealers, private company vehicle maintenance shops, garages, service stations, and city, county, and state governments.
Scrap tire processor means any person who is approved by the Environmental Protection Division to receive scrap tires from scrap tire generators or scrap tire carriers for the purpose of scrap tire processing.
Scrap tire sorter means any person, other than the original scrap tire generator, who handles mixed tires by separating used tires and retreadable casing from scrap tires.
(b) The owner or occupant of any premises shall be responsible for the sanitary handling and disposal of all scrap tires on the premises used or occupied by such person.
(c) It shall be unlawful to cause, suffer or allow the dumping of scrap tires at any place including, and without limitations, in or on any public highway, road, street, alley, or thoroughfare, including any portion of the right-of-way thereof, any public or private property or any waters unless the property is designated by the City Council and the State Environmental Protection Division (EPD) for the collection or disposal of scrap tires and the person is authorized to use such property. The scrap tires must be placed into a receptacle or container installed specifically for such property and the property has a valid solid waste handling permit or other applicable identification numbers, and approvals and/or permits issued by the State Environmental Protection Division when required.
(d) All persons defined as scrap tire generators, scrap tire carriers, scrap tire processors, including scrap tire sorters, and retail tire dealers shall be subject to rules as defined in Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. ch. 391-3-4 et seq. of the Georgia Rules for Solid Waste Management, as amended, and handle scrap tires in accordance with the provisions of the Georgia Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Act (O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq.) and the Georgia Rules for Solid Waste Management, Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. ch. 391-3-4 et seq., as amended, applicable to solid waste, except where provisions of this section are more stringent, in which case the provisions of this section shall be applicable unless preempted by State law.
(e) It shall be unlawful for any person in a residential zone to accumulate any amount of scrap tires on or around property, which they own or occupy.
(f) A retail scrap tire dealer may hold up to 100 scrap tires per garage bay in storage, up to a maximum of 1,000 scrap tires. One scrap tractor tire is equivalent to ten passenger tires; One semi tire is equivalent to five passenger tires. All tires must be stored in an enclosed structure.
(g) Tires must be stored in covered or enclosed areas to prevent the accumulation of water.

(1) The court may order the publication of the names and photographs of persons convicted of violating this section;
(2) The court may order the person convicted hereunder to repair or restore property damaged, or pay damages resulting from such violations, or perform public service related to the repair or restoration of property damaged by the violation;
(3) In case of a tire dump, the property owner, contractor, developer, builder or other person responsible for the property shall, upon conviction, cause the property to be cleaned and to come into full compliance with this section. The City Council shall not be responsible for any costs of cleanup or remediation;
(4) The expenses incurred by the City Council for cleanup, enforcement of violations and penalties shall be chargeable to the person convicted hereunder, such expenses, including, but not limited to, court costs, filing fees, special investigations, mutual aid assistance from other agencies and other costs necessary for the reasonable enforcement of this section;
(5) In addition to actions filed by the City Council for violations of this section, any State or federal agency may independently file separate or concurrent charges within their respective applicable authority and seek conviction within a court of competent jurisdiction;
(6) Enforcement of this section shall be the responsibility of the Mayor, Code Official and/or designee; and
(7) Any person authorized to enforce this section shall be empowered to enter any property, upon reasonable cause, at reasonable or necessary times in order to properly inspect for violations of this section, subject to the condition that to allow entry onto private property for inspection, the alleged violation of this section must be visible from a public road or right-of-way, or upon said person having received a valid complaint alleging a violation of this section, or by a judge's order upon said person having received information/allegations that constitute reasonable suspicion that a serious unlawful act or threat to the health and safety of the community and/or the environment has occurred or is about to occur.

Failure of owner or occupant to remove and correct any such accumulation of refuse shall be deemed a violation of this article.
(4) Junk. It shall be unlawful for any person to place or leave outside any building or dwelling any dilapidated furniture, appliance, machinery, equipment, building material, junked motor vehicle, or other item which is either in a wholly or partially rusted, wrecked, junked, dismantled or inoperative condition, and which is not completely enclosed within a building or dwelling. Any such item or items which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of ten days after notice of violation of this section shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject of being removed from the property by the City without further notice. This shall not apply to authorized junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning, or salvaging of equipment or furniture, if such establishment has sealed such equipment to the extent that it cannot be entered by any person without the consent of the establishment.
(5) Scavenging. No person other than the owner thereof, or an agent or employee of the Mayor, shall interfere with any container placed for the purpose of storing refuse pending collection, or remove or take any of the contents thereof, or remove any such container from the location where the same shall have been placed by the owner thereof.
(Code 2003, § 4-2015; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-15; Ord. of 9-3-1991)
627:
(a) All commercial establishments shall store their refuse in containers as specified herein so as to eliminate wind-driven debris and unsightly litter in and about their establishments. Approved methods of containerization include refuse receptacles, bulk containers and detachable containers. Spillage and overflow shall be immediately cleaned up by said establishment when and as it occurs.
(b) All commercial establishments shall have a bulk container unless their refuse and trash can be suitably contained in two 96-gallon containers to be picked up twice each week.
(c) Commercial customers shall be charged the amount established by the City for each extra can or each extra pickup.
(Code 2003, § 4-2016; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-16; Mo. of 9-13-1993)
628:
All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash. The number of containers necessary for each area shall be as required to maintain clean, neat and sanitary premises, as directed by the Mayor. The owner of the premises and the occupant thereof shall jointly and severally maintain surveillance to insure that all litter is placed in the proper container and the area is kept clean.
(Code 2003, § 4-2017; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-17)
629:
All construction and demolition contractors shall provide on-site refuse receptacles, bulk containers, or detachable containers for loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials, and other trash produced by those working on the site. The site shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number of refuse receptacles, bulk containers, or detachable containers shall be determined by the size of the job. Dirt, mud, construction materials or other debris deposited upon any public or private property as a result of construction or demolitions shall be removed by the contractor upon completion of the construction.
(Code 2003, § 4-2018; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-18)
630:
All occupants or operators of a residence, apartment, mobile home, motel or small office building shall place their refuse containers containing their refuse either at the curbside on a street adjacent to their property, or on their property immediately adjacent to an alley, on the days designated by the Mayor for pickup.
(Code 2003, § 4-2019; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-19)
631:
(a) Residential. Garbage and household trash accumulated by residences shall be collected one time each week. Oversize household trash, yard trash, and tree and shrubbery trimmings shall be collected one time each week at curbside, as specified herein.
(b) Commercial establishments. Service to commercial establishments shall be two times each week.
(c) Holidays. Collections shall not be made on the following holidays, unless otherwise specified by the Mayor: New Year's Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day, or on any other day designated by the Council as a holiday.
(d) Industrial waste. Industrial waste shall be collected, removed and disposed of by the operator of the factory, plant or enterprise creating or causing same.
(e) Hazardous refuse. No hazardous refuse shall be placed in any receptacle used for collection of refuse by the City.
(f) Dead animals. Small dead animals will be collected by the City during operating hours of the City landfill, provided the body is in a location accessible to the collector. Owners of large dead animals shall be responsible for their removal and disposal.
(g) Building materials. The City shall not be responsible for the collecting or hauling of building material originating from private property preliminary to, during or subsequent to the construction of new buildings, alterations or additions to existing buildings of whatever type or from demolition of existing structures. Such material shall be removed by the owner of the property or by the contractor.
(h) Hazardous or liquid wastes. Hazardous or liquid waste, or highly combustible industrial waste, shall not be disposed of in the City's landfill.
(Code 2003, § 4-2020; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-20; Mo. of 9-3-1991)
632:
(a) Contagious disease refuse. The removal of clothing, bedding or other refuse from homes or other places where highly infectious diseases have prevailed shall be performed under the supervision and direction of the County Health Department. Such refuse shall not be placed in containers for City collection.
(b) Hypodermic instruments. No person shall dispose of or discard any hypodermic syringe, hypodermic needle, or any instrument or device for making hypodermic injections before first breaking, disassembling, destroying or otherwise rendering inoperable and incapable of reuse, such hypodermic syringe, needle, instrument or device, and without safeguarding the disposal thereof by wrapping or securing same in a suitable manner so as to avoid the possibility of causing injury to the collection personnel.
(c) Cardboard boxes and cartons. Prior to depositing refuse for collection in authorized containers or receptacles or in commercial containers, the person disposing of any such boxes or cartons, or the person in charge of the premises, shall collapse all cardboard boxes and cartons.
(Code 2003, § 4-2021; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-21)
633:
A fee as established by the City shall be paid each month, per garbage can, to the City for the collection of garbage.
(Code 2003, § 4-2022; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-22; Mo. of 9-5-2000)
634:
(a) The Mayor or inspectors designated by the Officer, shall substantiate complaints of violations of any provisions of this article. They shall determine if there has been a violation and initiate requests for compliance with this article, by the person violating the article.
(b) The Mayor or designated inspectors shall be authorized to sign a complaint against said violator with the City Police Department.
(Code 2003, § 4-2023; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-23)
635:
It shall be unlawful for any person to put household garbage, trash or any other waste in a commercial dumpster within the City without permission from the owner of said dumpster.
(Code 2003, § 4-2025; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-25)
636:
It shall be unlawful for any person to remove any article, trash or other material from any commercial dumpster without permission from the owner.
(Code 2003, § 4-2026; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-26)
637:
It shall be unlawful for any person to scatter material from a commercial dumpster around the commercial dumpster site and anyone doing this shall be subject to the penalty as provided for in Section 1-7.
(Code 2003, § 4-2027; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-27)
640:
All domestic and other acceptable refuse shall be delivered and deposited at authorized disposal sites in accord with the directions and orders of the Mayor, or representative, in charge of operations; except, however, privately operated sites may be used for the sanitary disposal of industrial wastes or other specified waste upon the approval of the Mayor, and upon the issuance of appropriate disposal permits, as required by the regulations of the Georgia Department of Public Health, Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. ch. 511-3-4, entitled "Solid Waste."
(Code 2003, § 4-2042; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-42)
641:
(a) Public sites approved for the disposal of refuse shall be designated by appropriate signs posted near the roadside at the location of the Ocilla-Irwin County Landfill.
(b) Such sites shall be maintained in use until permanently closed, at which time additional authorized sites shall be opened and publicized by posting and through the press.
(Code 2003, § 4-2043; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-43)
642:
Authorized public disposal sites shall be operated Monday through Friday of each week, with the exception of the holidays listed in Section 44-39(c), from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., inclusive. During such hours, acceptable refuse generated in the City shall be received for disposal from any resident of the City.
(Code 2003, § 4-2044; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-44)
643:
No person shall enter a disposal site except when an attendant is present and during the hours and days prescribed in Section 44-66. All materials delivered and deposited for disposal on the grounds or disposal sites shall be the property of the City.
(Code 2003, § 4-2045; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-45)
644:
No person shall be permitted to scavenge or reclaim any refuse which has been delivered to a public disposal site for disposal.
(Code 2003, § 4-2046; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-46)
645:
(a) Domestic refuse. The following types of refuse shall be classed as "domestic refuse" and shall be accepted for disposal:
(1) Garbage, as defined in Section 44-21.
(2) Refuse, as defined in Section 44-21.
(3) Building materials, as defined in Section 44-21.
(4) Business trash, as defined in Section 44-21.
(5) Household trash, as defined in Section 44-21.
(b) Industrial waste. The following types of waste shall be classed as "industrial waste" and shall not be accepted for disposal:
(1) Industrial waste, as defined in Section 44-21.
(2) Hazardous refuse, as defined in Section 44-21.
(3) Building materials, as defined in Section 44-21, shall be accepted for disposal upon payment of a fee which shall be determined by the Mayor, and shall be paid at the time such material is accepted for disposal.
(Code 2003, § 4-2047; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-7)
646:
There will be charged and collected a fee in the amount established by the City for industry and commercial companies when dumping garbage, trash or waste at the City of Ocilla-Irwin County Landfill.
(Code 2003, § 4-2048; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-48)
647:
There will be charged and collected a fee for commercial haulers for hire when dumping garbage, trash, or waste at the City of Ocilla-Irwin County Landfill. Such fee shall be in the amount established by the City.
(Code 2003, § 4-2049; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-49)
648:
It is prohibited for any waste or trash coming from outside the County to be carried and dumped at the landfill and employees at landfill shall not accept such waste or trash.
(Code 2003, § 4-2050; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-50)
649:
(a) No person shall set fire to, or burn any papers or other refuse deposited at any disposal site or on the grounds thereof.
(b) No garbage or other materials, from which offensive odors emanate during combustion, shall be burned outside of any building.
(Code 2003, § 4-2051; Ord. of 7-10-1990, § 4-51)
652:
Council shall provide each year for working and keeping in good order the streets and sidewalks of the City, by contract or otherwise. The Public Works Director shall see that all ordinances are properly observed and enforced.
(Code 2003, § 4-1001)
653:
No person shall lay out, extend or alter any street, lane or open square without the consent of the Council at a regular meeting, and any application of this kind shall be published one month before a final action of the Council is taken thereon.
(Code 2003, § 4-1002)
654:
Surveys for the establishment, streets and sidewalks shall be made by the Public Works Director, who shall have supervision and control over working of the streets and sidewalks of the City.
(Code 2003, § 4-1003)
655:
No person shall make any excavation or opening or dig any ditch, trench, tunnel or hole in, along, across or under any street, sidewalk or other public place for the purpose of laying or placing therein any pipe, wires, poles or for any other purposes, unless a written permit therefor has been issued by the Council, provided that a permit shall not be required where such work is performed under a contract with the City but in the event such work requires a sidewalk or street to be wholly or partially obstructed, the person shall notify the Clerk, the streets and lanes and sanitation department and the police department at least two hours before obstructing the sidewalk or street, unless prevented by sudden emergency.
(Code 2003, § 4-1004)
656:
All persons desiring a permit in order to make an opening in any street or sidewalk, as set forth in Section 4-1004, shall make written application therefor, which application shall show the location of the proposed opening, the purpose therefor and the approximate number of square yards of surface to be cut. Such application shall be accompanied by a fee established by the Council.
(Code 2003, § 4-1005)
657:
Any person obtaining a permit as provided for in Sections 46-4 and 46-5 agrees, as a condition of the issuance of the permit, to indemnify and hold harmless the City against any claims or expenses, including attorney's fees, for bodily injury or property damage for accidents or occurrences arising out of the person's operations.
(Code 2003, § 4-1006)
658:
When any part of any street, sidewalk, alley or other public place of the City shall be torn or dug up for any purpose, the person making such excavation or opening shall have the duty of refilling such excavation or opening so as to restore it to essentially the same condition that existed prior to the excavation or opening and such refilling shall be done in accordance with the standards and specifications issued by the Council.
(Code 2003, § 4-1007)
659:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation who obtains a permit under this chapter to do any excavation of any kind which may create or cause a dangerous condition in or near any street, alley, sidewalk or public place of the City without placing and maintaining proper guard rails and signal lights or other warnings at, in or around the same, sufficient to warn the public of such excavation or work, and to protect all persons using reasonable care from injuries on account of same.
(Code 2003, § 4-1008)
